metadata.description: Per-environment flash and RAM build-size budgets for protoArtoo firmware
notes: Flash: binary image size (.bin file) to fit in the OTA partition (from partitions/*.csv app0/app1 size field)
RAM: static allocation (.data + .bss sections from linker via size -A), not heap or PSRAM

dram_limit_bytes: length of the linker's static-DRAM segment (dram0_0_seg in the generated memory.ld) under the platform's current configuration - informational only, no tool reads it. artoo-esp32=180736B now that Bluetooth is compiled out (it read 124580B while the BT controller reserved its window); esp32-p4=327680B
Budgets set with deliberate headroom to prevent reflexive raises on legitimate commits
Env-to-platform classification in 'platforms' registry; Makefile/slice_verify.py/check_build_budgets.py all consume it

platforms.esp32p4.envs must list EVERY platformio.ini env whose resolved platform is the P4 one (test_build_budgets.py checks this against platformio.ini): a P4 env missing here builds in the artoo-esp32 core dir and swaps that Arduino core in place. Only envs with an entry under 'envs' below are size-checked

Baseline measurements recorded with commit SHA (git cat-file -t to verify); baseline_* fields are informational only - check_build_budgets.py and slice_verify.py enforce flash_budget_bytes, flash_ceiling_bytes and ram_budget_bytes, never the baselines

Baseline method: flash = .pio/build/<env>/firmware.bin size; RAM = .data + .bss from the platform size tool (-A) on firmware.elf, i.e. slice_verify.get_build_sizes(); measured on a clean tree at the recorded commit (no -dirty stamp)

artoo_esp32.budget_rationale: Measured 1,391,856 B flash (87.0% of the budget, 81.7% of the partition) and 100,900 B static RAM at baseline_measured_at, where the Framework Envelope in platformio.ini compiles out the framework facilities this controller does not offer. Against the 1,596,112 B / 102,600 B image built from the same packages at the parent commit that is -204,256 B flash and -1,700 B RAM. Hard ceiling at 1,671,936 B (partition 1,703,936 - 32,000 B reserve for OTA headers/metadata). Flash budget stays at 1,600,000 B: the recovered bytes are headroom for in-flight work, not a new floor. The RAM budget (110,000 B until the raise recorded at the end of this note) is a heap-headroom figure, not a percentage of dram_limit_bytes - static .data+.bss shares the DRAM segment with the heap, and the request-admission floors in include/web_admission.h are calibrated against the largest free block, so a static byte saved is a heap byte gained. Compiling out Bluetooth widened the linker's static-DRAM segment from 124,580 to 180,736 B, but the firmware already released the Bluetooth region to the heap at boot via esp_bt_controller_mem_release(), so the real ceiling this budget guards has not moved. RAM budget raised 110,000 -> 112,000 B on 2026-09-10 (operator decision, epic #175) to carry ONE deliberate spend: the addressed Servo Output row table (#338), 24 rows x up to four Part ids at 13 B each plus the fixed fields, measured at 770 B with a single Part slot and projected at about 1,706 B with four. Sized to that spend and no rounder: the figure above is heap headroom, so every byte added here is a byte the admission floors in include/web_admission.h no longer have, and the runtime evidence for those floors is g_webRefusedHeapFloor / g_webRefusedHeapFloorDiag on a board rather than anything a build can show. The next raise is owed the same arithmetic.
artoo_esp32.fs_budget_rationale: DERIVED, NOT RATCHETED (#382, 2026-09-13). The filesystem partition holds two things that compete for the same 160 blocks: this web image and the builder's Learned Sequences, which the firmware writes to /seq at runtime. So the budget is what the partition can give the image while every sequence the firmware promises still fits: 160 blocks, minus nine full sequences, minus the free space the tenth save demands. SEQ_STORE_MAX is 10 (include/seq_store_index.h) and a file is at most 12 KB here (PA_SEQ_FILE_MAX_KB, include/seq_store_util.h); a save is refused unless free >= 2 x 12 KB + the file (src/seq_store_util.cpp), so the tenth save needs 36,864 B = 9 free blocks. Nine 12,288 B files in /seq cost 37 blocks, not 27: littlefs adds CTZ skip-list pointers that push a three-block file into a fourth, plus the directory. Measured by writing them into the real image with the platform's own littlefs-python parameters (block 4096, read/prog 1, cache 4096, lookahead 32, block_cycles 500, name_max 64, disk 2.1, a 4-byte mtime attribute per entry) and counting non-erased blocks. 160 - 37 - 9 = 114 whole blocks = 466,944 B. A test holds every filesystem figure here to whole 4,096 B blocks, because 470,016 B (the budget until now) was 114.75 blocks and its rationale called it 115. The image above that ceiling is not an image that is too big to flash, it is an image that takes the builder's sequence storage: at 113 blocks, the image this replaces, exactly ten full 12 KB sequences fit under the save rule and the eleventh was refused, so the sixteen-sequence cap was never reachable; at 77 blocks nineteen fit. (Commit 2efd03f4's message says the image ran out before the fifteenth; that count wrote files without the save floor and is wrong.) THE BASELINE: 315,392 B in 77 blocks at fs_baseline_measured_at, imaged with -t buildfs (46 staged files, 224,317 B of content), from 113 blocks at b2467053. Two changes bought the 36 blocks: shell delegates no longer inline the Page Recovery View kernel (11 copies, 113 -> 103 priced; ADR 0048 amendment) and tools/gzip_fsdata.py minifies JS and CSS with esbuild before gzipping (-> 77). An image that trips this budget is a decision about sequence storage, not a routine raise: raising it means lowering SEQ_STORE_MAX or the per-file cap with it, and the arithmetic above is redone. The ratchet history this replaces (100 -> 111 -> 114 blocks, 2026-09-12) is in this file's git log.

firebeetle2_bringup.budget_rationale: First-flash bringup env with minimal source filter (src/ excluded). Hard ceiling at 3,113,728 B (partition 3,145,728 - 32,000 B reserve for OTA headers/metadata). Baselines measured from the build artifacts at baseline_measured_at (see metadata notes). The earlier 321,774 B figure stamped 8fea3c7 is not reproduced by rebuilding 8fea3c7 with the current P4 packages (334,448 B, identical to now), so that delta is package- or method-side, not a source change. Budgets set above measured values to accommodate full firmware adaptation (tracked by #188/#189).

firebeetle2.budget_rationale: Full firmware: compiles all of src/ against P4 toolchain for production deployment. Hard ceiling at 3,113,728 B (partition 3,145,728 - 32,000 B reserve for OTA headers/metadata). RAM budget raised 100,000 -> 112,000 B on 2026-09-13 (#256 reopen): tools/slice_verify.measure_static_ram at baseline_measured_at reads 107,662 B (.dram0/.dram1 .data+.bss), 7,662 B over the old 100,000 B tripwire. That overrun pre-dates every Wave 0 slice (register row 2 on #381); the 61,214 B baseline stamped at 94880ee was a much older image and nothing re-measured this row while the firmware grew, because the slice gate walks artoo_esp32 only. 112,000 B is sized to the measured figure plus 4,338 B of headroom for in-flight work, the same order as the artoo-esp32 110,000 -> 112,000 raise, not rounded to a comfortable 120,000. Task stacks are xTaskCreate heap and do not appear here. Hardware DRAM (dram_limit_bytes 327,680) is nowhere near. The next raise is owed the same arithmetic. Flash budget stays at 2,000,000 B (measured 1,838,688 B, 91.9%).
firebeetle2.fs_budget_rationale: Measured 397,312 B at fs_baseline_measured_at -- byte for byte what artoo_esp32 measures, because one data/ image is still built for both, which is the whole reason #382 exists: this board has 9,957,376 B free and carries the 4 MB board's filesystem. Ceiling is the whole 10,354,688 B partition. Budget at 1,048,576 B is deliberately loose and guards a different thing from artoo_esp32's: with 9.5 MB spare there is no scarcity here, so this number exists to catch an accident -- a build that images something enormous -- not to ration. It is expected to rise when each file declares which environments carry it and the default asset set's photographs land here and not on the legacy set (ADR 0065).
